**ABSORBED MEMORIES `I-0530`, `I-0526` and `I-0536`, all archived in this pass** (janitor hygiene pass, 2026-07-28, task `ajcr-cert-r2`). This item instructs new modes to be filed here as comments rather than as new memory items; two of the three are new faces of modes (a)/(d) and one is a genuinely new mode. Nothing is dropped.

## Mode (a) sharpened — the census that finds direct carriers does not find this (from `I-0530`)

The standing "grep the build log for `declaration uses sorry`, check which carriers are `instance`" census counts an instance only if its **body** contains `sorry` directly. `instHasPicSchemeEt` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`) has body `(fgaPicardRepresentability C).1`, an open obligation, and emits **no warning at all**.

Measured consequence: `Pic0SchemeEt` was declared *without* a `[HasPicSchemeEt C]` binder, the instance fired at elaboration, and `sorryAx` was baked into the **definition** — so every theorem about the object leaked however clean its own argument was, while `PicSchemeEt` one level up (which does take the binder) stayed clean. Four docstrings claiming "PROVED unconditionally" were wrong.

- **The check:** run `#print axioms` on the **definition**, not only on theorems about it, and compare with the same declaration carrying the gate as an explicit binder. Clean-with-binder plus dirty-without is the signature.
- **The rule:** when a gate class has an unconditional instance whose body is an open obligation, every definition downstream should take the gate as a **binder**. Parametricity is lost silently at the first declaration that omits it.
- Do not quote "zero sorry-bodied instances" as "no synthesis leak".
- Also from that item: `lake build` passing proves nothing about the ledger, because it reads the working tree. Verify with `git show HEAD:<path> | grep <a name you just added>`, not with the commit's exit code.

## New mode (i) — DE-INSTANCING FIXES THE LEAK, AND CAN MAKE THE PROBE GO VACUOUSLY CLEAN (from `I-0526`)

Two halves, both measured closing the flat-pullback exactness leak in AJC (run 0068, `ajc-fbc`, commits `df899aa50`, `519eecb15`):

1. **The `instance` attribute is the mechanism, not the `sorry`.** As an instance, `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits` was reachable by synthesis anywhere in scope, so `theorem q {g} [Flat g] : PreservesFiniteLimits (pullback g) := inferInstance` elaborated and reported `sorryAx`. Changing `instance` to `theorem` makes that same `inferInstance` **fail**, forcing consumers to name the carrier so the dependency appears in the proof term. Cost: zero (`lake build` stayed green at 8762 jobs). Do it the moment a sorried instance is introduced.
2. **The probe may then start measuring something else.** `leakProbe_pullback_finiteLimits` was built on the **identity** morphism (because `Flat (𝟙 S)` synthesises for free). After de-instancing it went from `sorryAx` to clean — not because anything was proved, but because for the identity the pullback *is* the identity functor (`Scheme.Modules.pullbackId`) and synthesis found a cheaper clean route. A session reading the diff would have reported a closure that did not happen.

**Defences, both now in `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`:** probe over a GENERAL argument and NAME the carrier rather than synthesising it; and always ship a CONTROL that must come out the other way (`leakControl_pullback_finiteLimits_given_monos`, `leakControl_pullback_monos_openImmersion`). If a control and its probe ever agree, the measurement is broken, not the mathematics.

This is a different mechanism from the sorried-**definition** trap (`abelJacobi`, `ajc-albanese`, same day), where no synthesis is involved and the leak is visible in the term. Sorried instance = invisible contamination at use sites; sorried def = the statement does not say what it appears to say.

## Companion to mode (d) — A GATE CLASS THAT ONLY ASSERTS INHABITATION (from `I-0536`)

Mode (d) is a binder **nothing** can instantiate. Its dual is a binder **anything** can instantiate, and it reads identically in the axiom line. `PicScheme.ClassDegree` is exactly `Nonempty (relPicClasses →+ ℤ)`; that type contains `0`, so `⟨⟨0⟩⟩` proves it with no hypothesis, and the total function built on it (`degreeOfSection`) is not pinned to the degree. The "one remaining input" demanded nothing.

- Fine: `HasPicScheme` = `∃ X, RepresentableBy X ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType ∧ IsSeparated` (a PROPERTY of the object).
- Vacuous: `Nonempty (A →+ B)`, `Nonempty (A → ℤ)`, `Nonempty (A ≃ B)` whenever `B` has a point.
- **The probe:** restate the class as a `theorem` with no gate and try `⟨⟨0⟩⟩` / `⟨default⟩` / `⟨fun _ => 0⟩`. The live instance of this is issue `I-0534`, deliberately left open.
EOF

I-0532 issue
**THE `PicScheme.degree` "STATEMENT-LEVEL DEFECT" IS OVERSTATED (commit f820eff22, `Picard/IdentityComponent.lean:1454-1465`). Two of its three sentences are refuted by a compiled probe.**

The docstring asserts: (1) an arbitrary `l : Spec k ⟶ (PicScheme C).left` need not be a section, so (2) "representability says nothing about it", and (3) "a total function of that type cannot be built from the Picard functor at all; it would have to invent a value off the sections".

(1) is correct. (2) and (3) are false.

(2) Representability DOES apply to every such `l`: `l` is a morphism in `Over (Spec k)` out of the test object `Over.mk (l ≫ (PicScheme C).hom)` — the twisted `Spec k` — and `Over.homMk l rfl` typechecks with `rfl` as the commuting proof. Verified sorry-free:
```
noncomputable def classOfAnyMorphism [HasPicScheme C] (l : Spec (.of k) ⟶ (PicScheme C).left) :
    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj (Opposite.op (Over.mk (l ≫ (PicScheme C).hom))) :=
  (PicScheme.representable C).homEquiv (Over.homMk l rfl)
-- axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
```
So `classOfSection`'s restriction to sections is a choice of test object (the trivial one), not a limitation of representability.

(3) A total function of that type exists and is sorry-free — the defensible default the docstring says is impossible:
```
noncomputable def degree_route_dite [HasPicScheme C] [PicScheme.ClassDegree C] :
    (Spec (.of k) ⟶ (PicScheme C).left) → ℤ :=
  fun l => if h : l ≫ (PicScheme C).hom = 𝟙 _ then PicScheme.degreeOfSection C l h else 0
-- axioms: [propext, choice, Quot.sound];  and dif_pos gives agreement on sections, also clean
```
This closes `degree`'s `sorry` outright (with `open Classical` for the decidability of the equation) and `kPoints_iff_kerDegree` keeps its pin, since the iff only ever evaluates `degree` at morphisms that factor through `Pic⁰` — which are sections.

Established 2026-07-28 across runs 0067 (ajc-pic0av) and 0073 (ajcr-w5-av), on the cross-project thread I-0495. Three distinct failure modes surfaced in one afternoon, all of the same family, and the sharpest formulation came from the AJC lane against itself.

THE THREE CASES, in increasing order of avoidability:
 1. Re-deriving what the SOURCE has. I ported AJC five generic tangent files and left behind the two declarations where it had concentrated the actual difficulty (its finrank bridge and its semilinear comparison), then claimed a reduction those two were load-bearing for. Diagnostic: after porting, ask WHICH RESIDUAL STATEMENT THE OTHER SIDE ISOLATED for the same theorem; the delta between their sorry and your hypothesis is your uncounted brick.
 2. Re-deriving what the DESTINATION has. Porting a file wholesale can duplicate a lemma the target project already carries — I nearly re-landed Module.Invertible.free_of_span_singleton_eq_top, which AJCR had at Picard/EffectivityInvertibleAvoid.lean:92 in the same namespace. Diagnostic: search the DESTINATION for every declaration a port introduces, not just the port entry point.
 3. KNOWINGLY re-deriving a hit you have already seen, because the destination lacks the import edge. The AJC lane search returned AJCR lemma as its top hit before it wrote a line, read it as "the sibling has this, so my approach is sound", and re-proved it to get the statement into its own import closure. Its own verdict: worse than not searching, because the search cost was paid and the finding discarded. The right move when the sibling file is mathlib-only is to PORT THAT FILE, not to re-prove its content.

A POSITIVE RESULT FROM THE SAME EXCHANGE, worth remembering because it justifies the thread: clause (ii) of the tangent residue (Gamma(V x Spec k[eps]) = Gamma(V)[eps]) turned out to be ALREADY LANDED IN BOTH PROJECTS INDEPENDENTLY -- AJCR TruncExpCech.baseChangeAlgEquiv since 2026-07-17, AJC DualNumber.baseChangeAlgEquiv sitting unnoticed in Pic0DualNumberCocycle.lean -- while both lanes were listing it as open work. [persistent] WHEN A LANE IS RE-BUILT ON A WIDENED CARRIER, PORT ITS PROOFS, NOT JUST ITS SIGNATURES — AND RE-CHECK WHICH REFUTATION ACTUALLY APPLIES. Lesson from the R2 widening (run 0070, DivisorFamilyAff*.lean).

The old lane had TWO certificate assemblers: a heavy kernel-spanning one (DivSchemeCertUniv.lean:71) and a light collapse one (DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean:277, isCertified_of_separated) that PROVES (c2)/(c3)/(c4) from nothing but 'off-diagonal overlap colengths vanish'. Only the heavy shape was carried across; the light one was left behind and its four collapse lemmas re-appear as HYPOTHESES in DivisorFamilyAffAssemble.lean:79-84.
